column4: I'm working on this change history first. After that, the **Cleric Grudge** design and the leftover **talent description** audit are next.\n\nAnything marked "Developer build" only exists in my own test build until I say it's ready for Alpha Testers.

Armor that's too heavy now shows **exactly what it costs you**: evasion, movement speed and armor blocking lost for each missing point of strength. Identified armor shows the exact cost. Unidentified armor shows what it would cost if it's **unupgraded**, without revealing its real level.

**Developer build only:** the in-game menu has a **Bug Note** button. Type one line about what went wrong. It's saved on the phone with the time, floor, turn, class and seed, works without service, and goes into every bug report until you clear it.
This screen! The **Changes** button opens an SPD-style history with an entry for **every recorded build**, from the earliest builds to now. Use the arrows to page through the tabs.

Tapping the **magnifying glass** now searches anywhere in a room that still has a wall that could hide a door. It used to switch to Inspect unless you were standing next to that wall.\n\nRooms whose walls can't hide anything still tap to **Inspect**, and holding the button still does the opposite.
**Developer build only:** the game asks the phone for its **highest refresh rate** (144 Hz on the RedMagic). Bug reports record the rate that was asked for.

**Crashes:**\n- Fixed an **out-of-memory crash** during play. The Cleric Grudge was building the whole statistics catalog in the background. It now counts from a small per-run summary.\n- Fixed a crash when picking up an item with a **full backpack** (the swap window was built on the wrong thread).

**Developer build only:**
- A real-world **clock** in the top-right corner.
- **Frame time** under the clock, updated every frame.
- A **stutter probe** that logs every frame slower than 100 ms, with memory in use.
- A **memory spike watcher** that records every thread when the heap jumps.

**One rule for every search control.** The toolbar button, the chooser and the resume window all decide the same way: a full search is worth its turns near a wall that could hide a door, or in a room with **visible traps**.\n\nIn a trap room, tap now always searches and reveals hidden traps instead of falling back to Inspect.

- Rebuildable statistics caches are now **gzip-compressed**, so they take much less space.\n- The diagnostic journal no longer records every drag step. It keeps the **newest 8 MiB** instead of filling to 64 MiB.\n- The trace file is no longer rewritten on every drag frame.

Bug reports can now be **Standard** or **Extended**:
- Extended reports include an **action journal** between reports: moves, attacks, waits, setting changes, scenes, errors and memory milestones. Typed text is never recorded.
- It is **Off by default**. Turning it on shows the full privacy notice first, and turning it off erases the journal.
- Extended reports are saved as a **maximum-compression ZIP**. Standard reports are unchanged.
First build with the opt-in **Extended bug report** and its action journal.

This build merges two lines of work into one game:
- **R7:** new weapons and shields, full-pack swap, throw aiming, Greater Metamorphosis and the adaptive magnifier.
- **C485:** history, diagnostics and performance work, plus the newer seed-reuse scoring.

Passed **3,540 tests** with nothing failing.

Reading saved run history is faster and uses less memory. It reuses buffers, checksums and frame storage instead of allocating new ones for every entry, and stops holding old events when a log reopens.

Replaying a seed you've already played lowers that run's score. The formula went through several versions (cubic, depth-weighted, exponential per floor, then **exact 3/5 per reuse**).\n\nAll saved runs were **corrected retroactively** to the current version.

Many fixes to importing and exporting run history:
- Damaged, aliased or oversized archives are refused **without touching your existing history**.
- Error messages stay short instead of dumping whole files.
- Imports reuse memory instead of reading everything twice.

- Markdown reports keep literal brackets, backticks and asterisks.
- ZIP exports report their real size.
- Report saving no longer leaks a file or finishes twice when a worker fails.
- Diagnostic files always stay inside their own folder.
Android **memory-pressure** warnings are kept in the bug report's heap history, including across background/resume.

**Katana family:** Tanto, Wakizashi, Tachi and Nodachi.
**Shields, tiers 1-5:** Buckler, Targe and Kite Shield.

They use their own sprites and share the normal weapon drop weight. The Katana's guard now scales with upgrades.
**Scroll of Metamorphosis** is back to the original version. **Greater Metamorphosis** is a new spell that lets you pick from any talent in the tier.
Picking up an item with a full backpack now offers to **swap** it with something you're carrying, instead of leaving it on the floor.
Thrown weapons can be aimed at **any visible enemy**, not just the closest one.

The magnifying glass picks the right action for where you are:
- **Tap:** full search near a wall that could hide a door, Inspect elsewhere.
- **Hold:** the opposite.

Rooms that can't hide a door no longer offer Wall Search or get checkmarks. Wall Search won't start on floors without hidden doors.
- The difficulty bar now fades out with the hero select screen.\n- Stale Wall Search sessions from another floor are no longer offered.

**Remember interrupted wall searches:** Remember the wall, search position and completed manual searches after combat and saving. **Trust Level:** Added how much a record can be believed, and by whom.

**Trust Root:** Added the public keys the app trusts, each only for the purpose it was published for, with a validity window and a revocation list.

**Verifier:** Added checks a signature.

**Voting:** Added community voting primitives: one round has a fixed set of options and an open/close time; each player has at most ONE ballot per round (a new ballot replaces the old one until the round closes, so voting is idempotent and retried sends are harmless).

**Run Submission Factory:** Added the ONLY place where the player's local run facts are turned into something that could leave the device.

**Column Def:** Added one column of a dataset: what it is called, what kind of value it holds, who may see it and how values of several log segments of one run combine.

**Dataset:** Added a dataset's schema together with its rows, ready to be queried.

**Log Rows:** Added everything one log contributes: its meta and the rows of each dataset.

**Op:** Added what a filter does with its column.

**Query:** Added everything that decides what a UIMSD screen shows, as plain immutable data: which dataset, which scope, which filters, how it is sorted, which columns, whether it is grouped, and whether hidden information of FINISHED runs may be shown.

**Query Codec:** Added a query as text and back.

**Query Engine:** Added runs a Query over a Dataset.

**Query Result:** Added what a query produced, with everything needed to show it honestly: how many rows there were, what the scope and each filter cost, and how much of each column is actually known.

**Result Table:** Added a QueryResult laid out as a table of text, for any screen to draw: headers (what to call each column, whether tapping it sorts, how much of it is known) and lines of CellText.

**Row:** Added one row of a dataset.

**Row Builders:** Added turns one raw log into the rows of every dataset.

**Row Codec:** Added the compact binary form of one log's rows, for the row cache.

**Run segment totals:** Added combines the rows that one logical run recorded in several log segments into one row, column by column, following each column's Merge rule.

**Scope:** Added which rows are in play before any filter.

**Sort:** Added order by a column (or, in a grouped result, by an aggregate's id).

**Status Text:** Added the lines of the status strip above a UIMSD table: how many rows there are, what the scope and the filters left out, and how much of the data is actually known.

**Table Geometry:** Added where the columns and rows of a ResultTable go, in screen units.

**Statistics Model:** Added everything a UIMSD screen is, apart from the pixels: which view is open, the query being edited, the result, the page, and the moves between them (open a view, add a filter, click a header, follow a link, go back).
